PAYX.company_description: Outsourced payroll, HR and PEO/benefits provider for U.S. small and mid-sized businesses, now bulked up by its Paycor acquisition.

SCHW.company_description: Largest US discount brokerage and custodian, earning mostly net interest on client cash sweep plus trading and advisory fees across ~$12tn in client assets.

LPLA.company_description: LPL Financial is the largest US independent broker-dealer, operating a custody and advisory platform serving independent financial advisors.

CRWV.company_description: GPU neocloud that rents NVIDIA-centric AI training/inference capacity to AI labs and enterprises.

[2026-06] Broad enthusiasm for Natera's expanding clinical evidence (transplant/Prospera, oncology) underpinned the rally.

[2026-04-29] Fundamental support from Q3 FY26: revenue +7% to $5.94B, adj EPS $3.37 beat, FY26 guide raised to 6-7% revenue / 10-11% adj EPS growth.

AIR.PA.company_description: Airbus SE designs, manufactures, and sells commercial aircraft (A220, A320/A321neo, A330, A350, A380), helicopters, and defence/space systems; revenue is dominated by commercial aviation, with roughly 75% of EBIT from commercial aircraft…
bullets: [2026-02-19] Airbus guided 870 commercial aircraft deliveries for 2026 — below analyst consensus of ~880 — and its full-year FY2025 results were released by CNBC, causing an initial ~6% stock drop in February. By late March that dip had been fully recovered as investors refocused on the civil-aero upcycle narrative and the supply-chain recovery trajectory.

[2026-04-28] Q1 2026 results: revenue €12.7bn (down 7% YoY on weaker deliveries — 114 vs 136 a year earlier — partly due to ~20 aircraft held up by Chinese administrative issues). EBIT Adjusted fell 52% to €300m. But gross commercial orders surged to 408 aircraft (net 398 vs 204 in Q1 2025), the order backlog held at 9,037 units, and Defence & Space order intake jumped to €5.0bn (vs €2.6bn). Stock rose ~1% on the day, as investors looked through the delivery shortfall and focused on the record order intake and maintained 2026 guidance (€7.5bn EBIT Adjusted, ~870 deliveries). The result anchored the stock's re-rating relative to pure-defence peers.

[2026-Q2] Sector rotation away from pure-defence names (Ukraine ceasefire speculation, Germany scrapping the F126 frigate on 2026-06-24 wiping €11bn from Rheinmetall) drove a sharp flight-to-quality into civil-aero exposed names. Airbus, with ~75% of earnings from commercial aviation, was the primary beneficiary of this rotation — its 3m outperformance of +11.5% vs STOXX 600 mirrors a direct mirror-image of the pure-defence sell-off.

[2026-05-12] April monthly delivery/order report (Airbus: 67 deliveries, 28 gross orders; year-to-date 181 deliveries vs Boeing's 190) showed Boeing narrowing the gap, but Airbus maintained its YTD order lead with 436 gross orders vs Boeing's 297 — reinforcing narrative of durable commercial demand supporting a multi-year delivery ramp.

SAF.PA.company_description: Safran SA is a French aerospace, defence, and security group; its primary earnings driver is the CFM LEAP engine (a 50/50 JV with GE Aerospace) powering the A320neo and 737 MAX fleets, with the high-margin aftermarket (spare parts + rate…
bullets: [2026-02-13] FY 2025 results triggered a ~7.5% single-day rally (stock hit €330.1): adjusted revenue up 14.7%, recurring EBIT €5.2bn (+26%), FCF €3.9bn. Critically, Safran raised its 2028 medium-term targets dramatically — recurring operating income target lifted to €7.0–7.5bn (from €6.0–6.5bn previously), and cumulative FCF guidance raised to ~€21bn (from €15–17bn). This reset drove a sustained re-rating and provided the base from which the 3m rally launched.

[2026-04-23] Q1 2026 revenue: adjusted revenue €8,624m (+18.8% reported, +23% organic vs Q1 2025). LEAP engine deliveries surged 63% to 520 units (third consecutive quarter above 500); civil engine spare parts +29%; services +43% (driven by LEAP rate-per-flight-hour). CEO Olivier Andriès guided toward 'the high end' of 2026 targets (recurring EBIT €6.1–6.2bn, FCF €4.4–4.6bn). The blowout quarter — organic growth of 23% — was the single most important company-specific catalyst for the 3m move.

[2026-Q2] Sector rotation into civil-aero names: as Ukrainian ceasefire risk headlines hit pure-defence stocks (Rheinmetall, Saab, Hensoldt all -5% to -20% in individual sessions), Safran was a net beneficiary — its revenue mix is overwhelmingly civil (LEAP engines, aftermarket, Falcon landing gear, cabin equipment) with limited pure-defence weighting. The stock's +11.9% relative outperformance vs STOXX 600 is consistent with the broader rearmament-premium deflation trade.

[2026-mid-June] Safran stock flagged as a focus heading into the week after engine orders were reported at and around the Eurosatory/air show period — Jet2 selected CFM LEAP-1A for up to 71 A320/A321neo aircraft; Air India reaffirmed 210 A320neo LEAP commitments and 190 737 MAX LEAP commitments — incremental order flow reinforcing the multi-year LEAP delivery ramp narrative. (Note: Paris Air Show is biennial and was NOT held in 2026 — the next is June 2027.)

HO.PA.company_description: Thales SA is a French defence electronics, aerospace, and digital security conglomerate operating across five divisions: Defence & Security (largest, including radars, optronics, missiles, C2 systems), Avionics, Ground Transport Systems,…
bullets: [2026-03-03] FY 2025 full-year results: sales €22.1bn (+8.8% organic), EBIT margin 12.4%, FCF conversion 128%. Despite solid numbers, analysts flagged the 2026 guidance as 'cautious' — 6–7% organic growth and 12.6–12.8% EBIT margin — with the Cyber & Digital division declining 0.9% organically in 2025 (Imperva integration drag, sluggish payment-card volumes). Stock fell ~2% on the day. Berenberg reiterated 'hold' at €265; UBS was more bullish at 'buy'/€380. The cautious guidance set a negative tone entering the 3m window.

[2026-04-21] Q1 2026 trading update: revenue €5.3bn (+9.7% organic), orders €4.7bn (+27% organic with five large defence contracts vs one a year prior). Defence segment orders +75%. Despite another beat on orders, stock dipped ~2-3% on the day — a pattern of 'beat-and-sell' that reflects investors re-rating Thales away from a pure-defence premium. Cyber activity recorded a slight organic decline of (1.3)% in Q1 2026, reinforcing concerns about the Imperva integration timeline.

[2026-04-10 and throughout Q2] The core driver of Thales's -13.8% 3m move (-24.4% relative) is sector rotation: multiple Ukraine ceasefire/de-escalation headlines (notably April 10 when defence names dropped 3–6% in a session on peace-deal progress reports) disproportionately hit Thales versus Airbus/Safran because Thales is seen as predominantly a defence-electronics play. Unlike Rolls-Royce or Safran, Thales has no major civil-aero engine aftermarket stream to offset the de-escalation narrative. The rearmament premium built 2022–2025 deflated sharply.

[2026-06-15 to 19] Thales exhibited at Eurosatory 2026 (Paris-Nord Villepinte), unveiling SkyDefender integrated air-missile defence, RapidStriker counter-drone system, and a Renault joint venture 4 TROOP tactical vehicle. These are product showcases not contract announcements; no material positive stock catalyst emerged from the event, leaving the -14% 3m decline intact through the window close.

AM.PA.company_description: Dassault Aviation SA designs and manufactures the Rafale multi-role fighter jet (sold to the French Air Force and a growing list of export customers including India, Greece, UAE, Egypt, Indonesia) and the Falcon range of business jets; t…
bullets: [2026-03-04] FY 2025 annual results: net sales €7.42bn (+19% YoY), operating margin 8.6%, order intake €10.94bn (89% export). Rafale delivered 26 (beating 25-unit guidance); Falcon delivered 37 (missing 40-unit guidance for the third straight year). The Falcon miss was a recurring negative overhang — weak business-jet supply chain blamed, with the CEO warning French tax rises risk competitiveness vs US/Canadian rivals. Backlog €46.6bn (220 Rafale + 73 Falcon). 2026 guidance: sales ~€8.5bn, 28 Rafale, 40 Falcon. Despite record Rafale backlog, the stock's subsequent weakness reflects both the Falcon execution gap and the sector rotation.

[2026-Q2] Sector rotation: Dassault is perceived as ~60–70% defence (Rafale revenue) with a meaningful civil component (Falcon jets). As the European rearmament premium deflated on ceasefire headlines — with Rheinmetall, Saab, Hensoldt all hard down — Dassault was caught in the defence sell-off despite not being a pure-play armaments name. Its -9.2% 3m return (-19.8% relative) is less severe than the worst pure-defence names (RHM -34%) but materially worse than civil-aero peers (AIR, SAF both +22%).

[2026-06-24] Germany scrapped the F126 frigate programme (a €12.8bn Rheinmetall-led contract), triggering a broader European defence sector sell-off — Rheinmetall -18% to -20% intraday, with contagion to Saab, Hensoldt, Leonardo, BAE Systems. Dassault has no direct exposure to the F126 but was caught in the sector sell-off as the Germany news reinforced the narrative that European defence budget commitments may be softer/more volatile than the market had priced. This event falls at the very end of the 3m window (June 24–25) and likely explains some incremental downward pressure.

[2026-Q2] No new Rafale export contract was announced in the 3m window despite ongoing negotiations with UAE for a future Rafale version and discussions around India's potential 114-aircraft MRFA requirement. The absence of a newsflow catalyst, combined with the Falcon execution track record of missing delivery guidance three years running, left investors with limited positive ammunition against the defence-rotation headwind.

HAG.DE.company_description: Hensoldt is Germany's leading independent maker of radar, electronic-warfare, and optronics sensor systems for defense customers, selling mainly to the Bundeswehr and NATO allies.
bullets: [2026-06-24] Shares were hit alongside naval-exposed peers when Germany's Bundeswehr cancelled the ~€18bn F126 frigate program, sliding to a 52-week low of €63.12 around 25 June — management said it does not expect to change 2026 guidance from the cancellation, flagging only a minor revenue shortfall.

[2026-06-02] Management had already raised adjusted free-cash-flow guidance to ~50% of adjusted EBITDA (from ~40% previously), citing faster German government advance payments as procurement accelerates.

[2026-05-06] Q1 2026 results showed order intake more than doubling YoY to ~€1.5bn, pushing the backlog to a record €9.8bn (3.5x sales, book-to-bill 3.0x) — an order-momentum story reasserting itself after the F126 selloff, with the stock rallying ~17-20% off its low into next catalyst: H1 results due 2026-07-31.

R3NK.DE.company_description: RENK makes mission-critical transmissions and drivetrains for military vehicles (Leopard 2, Puma, Abrams) and naval propulsion, holding near-monopoly positions on most platforms.
bullets: [2026-06-24] RENK sold off alongside Rheinmetall and Hensoldt after Germany cancelled the F126 frigate program, part of a broad German-defence de-rating driven by fear that Berlin's procurement U-turn signalled wider budget/political risk, even though RENK's own naval exposure is limited to drivetrain content on the MEKO replacement ships.

[2026-06-26] RENK America won a five-year, up-to-$691m U.S. Army IDIQ contract for HMPT 800 hydromechanical transmissions (Bradley/AMPV platforms) — the fourth consecutive award cycle in the series — an idiosyncratic positive that only partly offset the broader sector slide at the time.

[2026-07-02] Shares rebounded together with the wider German defence complex as the market reassessed the F126 fallout as isolated to Rheinmetall's naval JV rather than a sector-wide procurement risk, recovering some of the ~11% lost over the prior week.
[2026-07-02] The bounce also lines up with pre-positioning ahead of the NATO Ankara summit (7-8 July), where NATO's Secretary-General has said billions in new defence contracts will be announced.

MTX.DE.company_description: MTU Aero Engines AG is Germany's leading aero-engine company — it holds risk-and-revenue shares in major civil turbofan programmes (GTF, GE9X, LEAP) and operates one of Europe's largest commercial MRO (maintenance, repair, overhaul) netw…
bullets: [2026-04-14] Kerrisdale Capital published a long thesis on MTU (bullish, not short): the fund argued the market was underpricing MTU's structural MRO margin expansion as the GTF engine fleet matures and shop-visit volumes surge. Kerrisdale noted GTF grounding counts had peaked (>720 at peak, declining), shop-visit ramp was irreversible, and 2025 earnings beat original guidance despite headwinds. The report catalysed institutional attention and contributed to a re-rating that had already begun on solid FY2025 numbers (+16% revenue, +29% adj. EBIT).

[2026-04-08] AeroDesignWorks acquisition announced: MTU acquired the DLR-spinoff drone propulsion specialist (~40 employees, gas turbines up to 400N thrust) to establish a UAV propulsion platform. The deal — price undisclosed — was read as MTU successfully bridging civil and defence growth vectors, giving the stock a dual 'civil MRO compounder + European defence exposure' narrative that attracted defence rotation capital at a time when pure-play land names were de-rating.

[2026-04-30] Q1 2026 earnings beat: adjusted revenue €2.244bn (+7% YoY), adj. EBIT €320m (+6%, margin 14.2%), FCF +18% YoY. GTF MRO revenues now 44% of commercial MRO (up from 34% in Q1 2025), MRO shop outputs +23% QoQ. Military revenue +25%. FY2026 guidance confirmed at €9.2–9.7bn revenue, €1.35–1.45bn adj. EBIT. Management noted zero cancellations or deferrals in MRO — emphasising the aftermarket's non-discretionary, contractually driven nature. Shares rallied on the print and held gains; FY order book hit €31.6bn (+7% YTD).

[2026-Q2] Sector rotation tailwind: as de-escalation headlines crushed Rheinmetall/Hensoldt/RENK, institutional capital rotated within the European A&D universe into civil-aerospace compounders (MTU, Airbus, Safran, Rolls-Royce). MTU's non-correlation to Ukraine newsflow — its MRO revenue is driven by global airline traffic, not defence procurement cycles — made it the natural beneficiary of this rotation. The +17.7% 3-month return vs. STOXX is predominantly a valuation re-rating (from ~20x to ~24x NTM EBIT) overlaid on genuine Q1 earnings momentum.

BA.L.company_description: BAE Systems is the UK's largest diversified defence prime, generating ~£30bn in annual revenue across air, maritime, land, and cyber/intelligence segments with major exposure to US DoD, UK MoD, and Saudi Arabia.
bullets: [2026-02-18] FY2025 results beat on fundamentals — underlying EBIT +12% to £3.32bn, sales +10% to £30.7bn constant-FX, EPS +12% to 75.2p, and a record £83.6bn order backlog (book-to-bill 1.2x) — but the stock barely moved; it had already rallied ~16% YTD and Jefferies had cut to Hold on Jan 30 at GBX 2,120, citing full valuation. The results confirmed strength but provided no upside surprise to deflate the rearmament premium baked in since late 2024.

[2026-04-10] Ukraine ceasefire/peace-deal headlines triggered the sharpest single-day leg down — BA.L fell ~3.3% on April 10 as Ukraine's chief negotiator Kyrylo Budanov signalled progress toward a settlement, sparking a broad European defence sector rotation out of pure-play rearmament names. BAE, with no civil-aero offset, bore the full brunt; the STOXX Europe Targeted Defence index fell >15% from its January 2026 peak through late May.

[2026-05-07] AGM/trading update (May 7, 2026) confirmed strong Q1 with record £75bn backlog, on-track FY guidance (sales growth 7–9%, EBIT growth 9–11%), and noted NATO spending tailwinds — but the market read this as 'no new upside' at a ~30x P/E. Stock continued to drift as investors questioned governments' ability to fund ambitious rearmament budgets given high borrowing costs.

[2026-Q2] Sector-wide de-rating: the Stoxx Europe A&D index ended the 3-month window ~15%+ below its January peak as sell-side consensus increasingly flagged 'most of the upside is in the price' — BA.L underperformed even within defence because it lacks any civil-aero or energy diversification to attract rotation buying. Relative performance of -27.4% vs STOXX 600 captures both the sector headwind and BAE's concentrated pure-defence positioning.

RR.L.company_description: Rolls-Royce Holdings is a UK engineering conglomerate primarily driven by its Civil Aerospace large widebody engine aftermarket (Trent family), complemented by a defence aero division (Typhoon/F-35), Power Systems (MTU marine/industrial)…
bullets: [2026-02-26] Record FY2025 results and transformational capital return announcement drove a ~7% share surge on the day — underlying operating profit +41% to £3.46bn (17.3% margin), FCF +38% to £3.3bn, net cash £1.9bn (from £475m a year prior). Management upgraded mid-term targets to £4.9–5.2bn operating profit and £5.0–5.3bn FCF by 2028, and announced a £7–9bn share buyback programme (2026–2028), including £2.5bn in 2026 alone — the largest buyback in company history. Civil Aerospace operating margin expanded to 20.5% from 16.6%, and the full-year 2026 guidance of £4.0–4.2bn operating profit / £3.6–3.8bn FCF was set.

[2026-04-30] AGM trading update reaffirmed all 2026 guidance; Q1 large engine flying hours grew 5% to 115% of 2019 pre-pandemic levels — at the top of the company's annual target range — demonstrating widebody aftermarket demand remains robust. Contracts for three SMR units at Anglesey (UK/GBE-N) and up to six reactors for ČEZ (Czech Republic) both confirmed in execution phase, generating 2026 revenues. Defence wins included MT30 marine gas turbine selection for up to 11 Australian Navy frigates. Shares continued to outperform on the view that RR has a unique triple-diversification (civil-aero turnaround + SMR optionality + defence) that insulates it from the pure-defence de-rating.

[2026-06-15] Rolls-Royce SMR selected by Videberg Kraft (Vattenfall/Industrikraft JV) to supply three 470 MWe reactors in Sweden — the first new nuclear in Sweden for 40+ years and the third European country to select RR SMR after UK and Czech Republic. The announcement came close to RR.L's all-time high of GBX 1,424 (reached June 17), adding credibility to a >£300bn global SMR addressable market thesis. Each new national selection de-risks the SMR business and raises the probability of further pipeline announcements.

[2026-Q2] RR.L bucked the European pure-defence selloff entirely because ~55–60% of earnings exposure is civil aerospace (which benefited from continued widebody recovery) and the buyback provides an ongoing price floor. The +28.3% total return in EUR vs -10.6% for STOXX 600 reflects both company-specific re-rating and active rotation into civil-aero/diversified names as investors trimmed pure-defence.

BAB.L.company_description: Babcock International is a UK government-focused defence and engineering services group, with major programmes in naval shipbuilding (Type 31 frigates), nuclear decommissioning, and aviation/emergency services.
bullets: [2026-02-06] Citi downgraded Babcock from Buy to Neutral, citing the stock had already rallied strongly and now offered only ~8% upside to their revised base-case target — a valuation-ceiling signal that front-ran the broader sector de-rating. This was followed by further analyst selectivity as the European A&D index rolled over from its January 2026 peak.

[2026-04-10] Caught in the same Ukraine peace-talk selloff that hit BAE — European defence stocks broadly fell 2–6% on April 10 as Budanov's ceasefire comments hit wires. Babcock, as a small-mid cap pure-play UK defence services name with even less liquidity and diversification than BAE, saw amplified selling; the FTSE 100 noted Babcock as among its biggest decliners on that session.

[2026-06-22] FY2026 full-year results (year-end March 31, 2026) delivered strong underlying metrics — organic revenue +8%, underlying operating profit +19% to £433m, margin +70bps to 8.2%, EPS +20%, dividend +15%, and a new £200m buyback — but shares fell ~5–6% because the headline was dominated by a £140m exceptional charge on the Type 31 frigate programme (rework and outfitting productivity issues on ships 1 and 2). The charge reduced reported operating profit to £293m and attributable net profit to £211m (from £247m prior year). Management noted lessons learned will reduce impact on ships 3 and 4, but the market focused on execution risk re-emerging.

[2026-Q2] The -15.7% total return (EUR) over the 3-month window reflects the combined weight of: (1) sector-wide European pure-defence de-rating on peace-deal risk, (2) a post-rally valuation reset after the stock had outperformed dramatically in 2024–2025, and (3) the June results charge delivering a fresh execution-risk discount. The Type 31 charge alone likely accounts for 5–7pp of the underperformance vs the index; the rest is shared with BAE as sector-level multiple compression.

LDO.MI.company_description: Leonardo is Italy's largest defence and aerospace prime, spanning helicopters, defence electronics, cyber/digital, and aerostructures.
bullets: [2026-07-07] European defence rallied hard into the NATO Ankara Summit (opened Tue Jul 7), where Sec-Gen Rutte pressed allies for 'concrete, credible' plans to hit the agreed 5% GDP target (3.5% core + 1.5% infrastructure) — sector-wide bid lifting Rheinmetall +16.4% and the primes 6-10% on the week.

[2026-07-07] Leonardo-specific: at the NATO Summit Defence Industry Forum it signed the first implementation phase of NATO's Protected Business Network digital-transformation program (alongside an Accenture NATO award), CEO Mariani framing it as a milestone for operational readiness — reinforcing its defence-electronics/digital growth story.

[2026-07-06] Momentum backed by fundamentals: record ~EUR 57bn backlog, revenue +11% and operating profit +18% YoY, with new orders +15% — Leonardo now one of the FTSE MIB's top performers, +17% YTD before this week's surge.

[2026-07-07] Move led peers on the week (+19.2%, +18.3% rel URTH) versus AIR.PA +9.3%, HO.PA +9.3%, AM.PA +9.7%, RHM.DE +16.4% — a broad defence bid with Leonardo out front on its own NATO contract news.

bullets: [2026-07-06] Announced agreement to acquire majority stakes in four underwater-tech firms (Next Geosolutions, WSense, Graal Tech, Defcomm) for ~EUR 600m (~$687m), creating the first vertically integrated subsea operator.

[2026-07-06] Guided the deals to lift 2026 pro-forma underwater-segment revenue above EUR 1.1bn with ~EUR 220m EBITDA, add >EUR 60m to group net profit, +13% pro-forma EBITDA and +40% pro-forma net profit.
[2026-07-06] Read as a decisive M&A pivot into marine drones and secure underwater communications for both commercial and defense end-markets, driving the +18.95% 5d move.

bullets: [2026-07-06] Canadian PM Mark Carney named TKMS preferred bidder to build the navy's new submarine fleet, selecting its Type 212CD over Hanwha Ocean's KSS-III.
[2026-07-06] Program covers up to 12 submarines with a whole-of-life value estimated above CAD/USD 100bn; contract negotiations to begin shortly and close by year-end, first four subs by 2034.
